customerJourneyStories.name: Adopt the marketplace for a first major renovation
customerJourneyStories.summary: A homeowner with an expensive, unfamiliar project adopts the marketplace only if it reduces uncertainty without creating a new loss of control over personal data or sales contact.

stages.narrative: A failing building element, high energy bill, comfort problem, move, or subsidy window creates urgency, while the homeowner has no trusted specialist to call.

The homeowner becomes aware of Solvari through search results, a renovation advice article, an affiliate form, a recommendation, or an acquired marketplace brand and recognizes an offer to compare vetted local specialists.

Before submitting anything, the homeowner checks whether the service is free, how many companies may make contact, how specialists are screened, how reviews work, what Solvari is responsible for, and whether sharing project and contact data feels proportionate.

The first bounded use is one real project request; the homeowner tests whether the form is understandable, consent is clear, confirmation is immediate, and the first contacts are relevant and respectful.
The homeowner returns to the request workspace to track responses, examine profiles and reviews, exchange messages, and compare proposals with the platform's guidance.

A good match, transparent follow-up, and credible handling of feedback make the marketplace the starting point for the next maintenance or sustainability project and something the homeowner recommends to others.

stages.narrative: Rising request volume, a new acquisition, inconsistent claim outcomes, or an automation incident exposes the cost of fragmented tools and local playbooks.
Through internal enablement, migration planning, a quality review, or a colleague's demonstration, the operator becomes aware of a unified console and the workflows it can replace.

Before relying on it, the operator compares decision coverage, local-policy support, data completeness, explainability, permissions, auditability, queue performance, and fallback behavior against existing tools and spreadsheets.
One category or acquired-brand queue runs in parallel, letting operators compare recommendations and outcomes while retaining the existing recovery path.
The console becomes the daily place for qualification, overrides, case handling, review integrity, lead claims, quality monitoring, and handoffs between specialist teams.
Operators stay when the console reduces manual work and inconsistent decisions, exposes automation errors early, and turns repeated cases into visible control improvements.
